steps.title: 이름 묻기
steps.goal: 이름을 묻고 말하고, 헤어질 때 인사하기
steps.scene_desc: 이삿날 아침, 아파트 5층 복도. 이삿짐 상자 옆에서 지우와 옆집 그레이스(화분을 든 채)가 처음 인사
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s your name?" (이름 묻기). Goal: 이름을 묻고 말하고, 헤어질 때 인사하기. Today's scene: 이삿날 아침, 아파트 5층 복도. 이삿짐 상자 옆에서 지우와 옆집 그레이스(화분을 든 채)가 처음 인사. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s your name?".

steps.when: 처음 만난 사람의 이름을 물을 때 써요.
steps.extra: 대답은 My name is ___. 또는 짧게 I’m ___.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What’s your name?" (이름이 뭐예요?). When to use it: 처음 만난 사람의 이름을 물을 때 써요. Note: 대답은 My name is ___. 또는 짧게 I’m ___.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "My name is ___.".

steps.extra: My name is Jiwoo. = I’m Jiwoo.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "My name is ___." (제 이름은 ~예요.). When to use it: 내 이름을 말할 때 써요. Note: My name is Jiwoo. = I’m Jiwoo.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "See you later!".

Expression 3 of 3: "See you later!" (이따 봐요! / 또 봐요!). When to use it: 헤어질 때 가볍게 하는 인사예요. Note: 더 짧게: See you! · Bye!
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Moving Day · 이삿날, 5층 복도에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Moving Day · 이삿날, 5층 복도에서

lines.en: Yes! Nice to meet you, Grace.
Nice to meet you, too. Take your time.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Moving Day · 이삿날, 5층 복도에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Grace: "Hi! Are you new here?" (안녕하세요! 새로 오셨어요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Yes. Hi!" (네. 안녕하세요!)
3. Grace: "I’m Grace. What’s your name?" (저는 그레이스예요. 이름이 뭐예요?)
4. Jiwoo: "My name is Jiwoo." (제 이름은 지우예요.)
5. Grace: "Jiwoo. J-I-W-O-O?" (지우요. J-I-W-O-O?)
6. Jiwoo: "Yes! Nice to meet you, Grace." (네! 만나서 반가워요, 그레이스.)
7. Grace: "Nice to meet you, too. Take your time." (저도 반가워요. 천천히 하세요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Thanks! See you later!" (고마워요! 이따 봐요!)
9. Grace: "See you later!" (이따 봐요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.title: Moving Day · 이삿날, 5층 복도에서

lines.en: Yes! Nice to meet you, Grace.
Nice to meet you, too. Take your time.

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Grace exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Grace (you): "Hi! Are you new here?" (안녕하세요! 새로 오셨어요?)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes. Hi!" (네. 안녕하세요!)
3. Grace (you): "I’m Grace. What’s your name?" (저는 그레이스예요. 이름이 뭐예요?)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "My name is Jiwoo." (제 이름은 지우예요.)
5. Grace (you): "Jiwoo. J-I-W-O-O?" (지우요. J-I-W-O-O?)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Yes! Nice to meet you, Grace." (네! 만나서 반가워요, 그레이스.)
7. Grace (you): "Nice to meet you, too. Take your time." (저도 반가워요. 천천히 하세요.)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "Thanks! See you later!" (고마워요! 이따 봐요!)
9. Grace (you): "See you later!" (이따 봐요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Grace. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: Grace checks how to spell Jiwoo’s name.
steps.teach:
True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Grace is new here.
2. Grace checks how to spell Jiwoo’s name.
3. Grace says, “See you later!”
The scene they are about:
1. Grace: "Hi! Are you new here?" (안녕하세요! 새로 오셨어요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Yes. Hi!" (네. 안녕하세요!)
3. Grace: "I’m Grace. What’s your name?" (저는 그레이스예요. 이름이 뭐예요?)
4. Jiwoo: "My name is Jiwoo." (제 이름은 지우예요.)
5. Grace: "Jiwoo. J-I-W-O-O?" (지우요. J-I-W-O-O?)
6. Jiwoo: "Yes! Nice to meet you, Grace." (네! 만나서 반가워요, 그레이스.)
7. Grace: "Nice to meet you, too. Take your time." (저도 반가워요. 천천히 하세요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Thanks! See you later!" (고마워요! 이따 봐요!)
9. Grace: "See you later!" (이따 봐요!)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: 이럴 때
이렇게 말해요
rows: My name is Jiwoo. / I’m Jiwoo.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What’s your name? / My name is ___. / I’m ___. Table (이럴 때 → 이렇게 말해요):
- 이름을 물을 때 → What’s your name?
- 이름을 말할 때 → My name is Jiwoo. / I’m Jiwoo.
- 철자를 말할 때 → J-I-W-O-O (한 글자씩)
- 헤어질 때 → See you later! / Bye!
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
‘~예요’는 be동사로 말해요.
My name *is* Jiwoo. 제 이름은 지우예요.
*I’m* Jiwoo. 저는 지우예요. (I’m = I am)

*my* name 내 이름 · *your* name 당신 이름
What’s *your* name? — *My* name is Grace.
errors: I’m(저는 ~예요)과 My name is를 섞지 않아요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- is · am: ‘~예요’는 be동사로 말해요. / My name is Jiwoo. 제 이름은 지우예요. / I’m Jiwoo. 저는 지우예요. (I’m = I am)
- my · your: my name 내 이름 · your name 당신 이름 / What’s your name? — My name is Grace.
Common mistakes on screen:
- My name Jiwoo. → My name is Jiwoo. (is를 빼지 않아요.)
- I’m name is Jiwoo. → My name is Jiwoo. (I’m(저는 ~예요)과 My name is를 섞지 않아요.)
- What your name? → What’s your name? (What’s = What is. ’s를 꼭 붙여요.)
- See you late! → See you later! (late는 ‘늦은’, later는 ‘나중에’예요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: is · am: ‘~예요’는 be동사로 말해요.My name is Jiwoo. 제 이름은 지우예요.I’m Jiwoo. 저는 지우예요. (I’m = I am)
my · your: my name 내 이름 · your name 당신 이름What’s your name? — My name is Grace.
mistakes: My name Jiwoo. → My name is Jiwoo.
I’m name is Jiwoo. → My name is Jiwoo.
What your name? → What’s your name?
See you late! → See you later!

steps.note: 예) Daniel → My name is Daniel. D-A-N-I-E-L. · 이름을 말하고 철자도 한 글자씩 말해 봐요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) Daniel → My name is Daniel. D-A-N-I-E-L. · 이름을 말하고 철자도 한 글자씩 말해 봐요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: Daniel → D-A-N-I-E-L | Chloe → C-H-L-O-E | Ben → B-E-N | Maya → M-A-Y-A.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What’s your name?" (이름 묻기); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What’s your name?" / "My name is ___." / "See you later!". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 인사하기: "Hi, I’m ___." (안녕하세요, ~예요., 친근); "Good morning." (좋은 아침이에요., 보통); "Nice to meet you, too." (저도 만나서 반가워요., 보통)
- 이름 다시 묻기: "Sorry, what’s your name again?" (죄송한데, 이름이 뭐라고 하셨죠?, 정중); "How do you spell that?" (철자가 어떻게 돼요?, 보통); "Just call me ___." (그냥 ~라고 불러 주세요., 친근)
- 헤어지기: "Bye!" (안녕!, 친근); "Take care." (잘 지내요., 친근); "Have a nice day!" (좋은 하루 보내요!, 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: first name · last name

영어는 이름을 먼저, 성을 나중에 말해요.
Kim Jiwoo → *Jiwoo Kim*
first name 이름 · last name 성
시간에 맞는 인사

A: Hi! What’s ___ name?   B: ___ name is Jiwoo.
A: Nice to ___ you!   B: See you ___!
낱말 상자: your · My · meet · later
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- first name · last name: 영어는 이름을 먼저, 성을 나중에 말해요. / Kim Jiwoo → Jiwoo Kim / first name 이름 · last name 성
- 시간에 맞는 인사: Good morning 오전 · Good afternoon 낮 12~6시 / Good evening 저녁 · Good night 잘 자요(헤어질 때만)
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Hi! What’s ___ name? B: ___ name is Jiwoo. / A: Nice to ___ you! B: See you ___! / 낱말 상자: your · My · meet · later
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: hello (안녕하세요), goodbye (잘 가요), morning (아침), afternoon (오후), evening (저녁), night (밤), name (이름), spell (철자를 말하다), meet (만나다), call (부르다, 전화하다), day (날, 하루), later (나중에).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: first (첫 번째의) — "first name 이름"; last (마지막의) — "last name 성"; nice (좋은, 반가운) — "Nice to meet you."; again (다시) — "Say it again."; also (또한, ~도) — "I’m also new here."; too (~도, 역시) — "Nice to meet you, too."; see (보다, 만나다) — "See you later!"; here (여기) — "I’m new here."; new (새로운) — "I’m new.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: How do you spell your name?
Do you have an English name?
See you later! / Bye! / Take care.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What’s your name?" (hint on screen: My name is ___. / I’m ___.)
- "How do you spell your name?" (hint on screen: J-I-W-O-O처럼 한 글자씩 말해요.)
- "Do you have an English name?" (hint on screen: Yes, it’s ___. / No, I don’t.)
- "What can I call you?" (hint on screen: Just call me ___.)
- "Say goodbye to me!" (hint on screen: See you later! / Bye! / Take care.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: How do you spell your name?
Do you have an English name?

steps.title: Jiwoo’s New Home
steps.text: Jiwoo has a new home. It is on the fifth floor. Her neighbor is Grace. Grace is kind. She says, “Take your time.” Jiwoo is *also* kind. She says, “See you later!” She is happy.
steps.gloss: home 집 · floor 층 · neighbor 이웃 · kind 친절한 · also ~도, 또한
questions: What floor is Jiwoo’s home on?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Jiwoo’s New Home". Text: "Jiwoo has a new home. It is on the fifth floor. Her neighbor is Grace. Grace is kind. She says, “Take your time.” Jiwoo is also kind. She says, “See you later!” She is happy." Words: home 집 · floor 층 · neighbor 이웃 · kind 친절한 · also ~도, 또한.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Who is Jiwoo’s neighbor?" / "What floor is Jiwoo’s home on?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘What’s your name?’으로 이름을 물을 수 있어요.
‘My name is ___.’로 내 이름을 말할 수 있어요.
‘See you later!’로 헤어질 때 인사할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘What’s your name?’으로 이름을 물을 수 있어요.
- ‘My name is ___.’로 내 이름을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘See you later!’로 헤어질 때 인사할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 오늘 기분
steps.scene_desc: 금요일 아침, 지우의 사무실. 하늘색 셔츠의 클로이가 밝게 손을 흔들고, 지우는 커피를 들고 조금 피곤한 얼굴

This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.

Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "How are you?" (오늘 기분). Goal: 안부를 묻고 내 기분을 말하기. Today's scene: 금요일 아침, 지우의 사무실. 하늘색 셔츠의 클로이가 밝게 손을 흔들고, 지우는 커피를 들고 조금 피곤한 얼굴. What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "How are you?".

steps.extra: 친구 사이엔 How’s it going?도 써요.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "How are you?" (잘 지내요? / 기분 어때요?). When to use it: 만났을 때 안부를 물어요. Note: 친구 사이엔 How’s it going?도 써요.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I’m ___.".

steps.extra: I’m happy. · I’m a little tired.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I’m ___." (~해요. (기분)). When to use it: 내 기분이나 상태를 말해요. Note: I’m happy. · I’m a little tired.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "What about you?".

steps.when: 대답한 뒤 상대에게 똑같이 물을 때 써요.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "What about you?" (당신은요?). When to use it: 대답한 뒤 상대에게 똑같이 물을 때 써요. Note: = And you?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Happy Friday · 금요일 아침, 사무실에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Happy Friday · 금요일 아침, 사무실에서

steps.title: Happy Friday · 금요일 아침, 사무실에서

lines.en: Ooh! Say it with me: “Happy Friday!”

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Chloe exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Chloe (you): "Good morning, Jiwoo! How are you?" (좋은 아침, 지우! 잘 지내요?)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "I’m a little tired. What about you?" (조금 피곤해요. 클로이는요?)
3. Chloe (you): "I’m so happy today!" (저는 오늘 정말 기뻐요!)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "Why?" (왜요?)
5. Chloe (you): "It’s Friday!" (금요일이잖아요!)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Oh, right! I’m happy, too." (아, 맞다! 저도 기뻐요.)

First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Chloe. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo is a little tired.
2. Chloe is sad today.
3. Today is Friday.

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: 기분
기본·조금
정말
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: How are you? / I’m ___. What about you? Table (기분 → 기본·조금):
- happy 기쁜 → I’m happy.
- tired 피곤한 → I’m a little tired.
- busy 바쁜 → I’m a little busy.
- hungry 배고픈 → I’m a little hungry.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
기분은 I’m 뒤에 그대로 붙여요.
*I’m* happy. *I’m* tired.
‘I happy’처럼 ’m을 빼지 않아요.

a little 조금 · very 아주 · so 정말
I’m *a little* tired. I’m *so* happy!
errors: a little은 기분 낱말 앞에 와요.
짧게 What about you? 또는 And you?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- I’m + 기분 낱말: 기분은 I’m 뒤에 그대로 붙여요. / I’m happy. I’m tired. / ‘I happy’처럼 ’m을 빼지 않아요.
- 얼마나? a little · very · so: a little 조금 · very 아주 · so 정말 / I’m a little tired. I’m so happy!
Common mistakes on screen:
- I happy. → I’m happy. (기분을 말할 땐 I’m.)
- I’m tired a little. → I’m a little tired. (a little은 기분 낱말 앞에 와요.)
- I’m feel good. → I feel good. / I’m good. (I’m과 feel을 같이 쓰지 않아요.)
- How about you are? → What about you? (짧게 What about you? 또는 And you?)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

I’m feel good. → I feel good. / I’m good.

steps.note: 예) tired / a little → I’m a little tired.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) tired / a little → I’m a little tired. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: tired → a little | happy → so | busy → very | hungry → a little.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "How are you?" (오늘 기분); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "How are you?" / "I’m ___." / "What about you?". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 대답하기: "I’m fine, thanks." (잘 지내요, 고마워요., 보통); "Not bad." (나쁘지 않아요., 친근); "Pretty good." (꽤 좋아요., 친근); "I’m okay." (괜찮아요., 보통)
- 묻기: "How’s it going?" (어떻게 지내요?, 친근)
- 반응하기: "Good to hear." (다행이네요., 보통); "Oh no. Are you okay?" (어머, 괜찮아요?, 보통); "I’m a little tired." (조금 피곤해요., 보통); "I’m so happy today." (오늘 정말 기뻐요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

A: How ___ you?   B: I’m a ___ tired. What ___ you?

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- How are you? 의 대답: 원어민은 대개 짧게 Good! / Fine. / Not bad.라고 하고 바로 And you?로 되물어요.
- 기분 짝꿍: happy ↔ sad · good ↔ bad · busy ↔ free / sleepy 졸린 · tired 피곤한
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: How ___ you? B: I’m a ___ tired. What ___ you? / A: I’m ___ happy! / 낱말 상자: are · little · about · so
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: happy (기쁜), sad (슬픈), tired (피곤한), sleepy (졸린), hungry (배고픈), busy (바쁜), fine (괜찮은), bad (나쁜), good (좋은), okay (괜찮은), well (건강한, 잘), today (오늘).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: little (조금, 작은) — "a little tired"; very (아주) — "very busy"; so (정말, 아주) — "so happy"; feel (느끼다) — "I feel good."; how (어떻게) — "How are you?"; about (~에 대해) — "What about you?"; thanks (고마워요) — "Fine, thanks."; right (맞는) — "Oh, right!"; Friday (금요일) — "It’s Friday!".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.
Yes, I’m very busy. / No, not really.
I’m happy on Fridays. / I’m happy on ___.
How are you? / What about you?
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "How are you today?" (hint on screen: I’m ___. / I’m a little ___.)
- "Are you tired today?" (hint on screen: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.)
- "Are you busy this week?" (hint on screen: Yes, I’m very busy. / No, not really.)
- "When are you happy?" (hint on screen: I’m happy on Fridays. / I’m happy on ___.)
- "Ask me how I am." (hint on screen: How are you? / What about you?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Chloe at Work
steps.text: Chloe works with Jiwoo. She is from Canada. Every morning, she says, “Good morning! How are you?” She is always happy. Jiwoo is sometimes tired. But Chloe makes her smile.
steps.gloss: work with ~와 같이 일하다 · every morning 매일 아침 · always 늘 · sometimes 가끔 · smile 웃다
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Chloe at Work". Text: "Chloe works with Jiwoo. She is from Canada. Every morning, she says, “Good morning! How are you?” She is always happy. Jiwoo is sometimes tired. But Chloe makes her smile." Words: work with ~와 같이 일하다 · every morning 매일 아침 · always 늘 · sometimes 가끔 · smile 웃다.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Where is Chloe from?" / "How is Chloe every morning?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘How are you?’로 안부를 물을 수 있어요.
‘What about you?’로 상대에게 되물을 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘How are you?’로 안부를 물을 수 있어요.
- ‘I’m ___.’으로 내 기분을 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘What about you?’로 상대에게 되물을 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 고마워요, 미안해요
steps.scene_desc: 토요일 오후, 이사 마지막 날. 아파트 5층 복도. 처음 만난 3층 이웃 벤이 무거운 상자를 들어 주고, 지우가 고마워하며 꾸벅 인사. 상자 하나가 벤의 발 옆에 떨어짐
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Thank you so much!" (고마워요, 미안해요). Goal: 고맙다·미안하다고 말하고 답하기. Today's scene: 토요일 오후, 이사 마지막 날. 아파트 5층 복도. 처음 만난 3층 이웃 벤이 무거운 상자를 들어 주고, 지우가 고마워하며 꾸벅 인사. 상자 하나가 벤의 발 옆에 떨어짐. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Thank you so much.".

steps.when: 도움을 받았을 때 마음을 담아 말해요.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Thank you so much." (정말 고마워요.). When to use it: 도움을 받았을 때 마음을 담아 말해요. Note: 짧게: Thanks a lot.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I’m sorry.".

steps.extra: 더 미안할 때: I’m really sorry.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I’m sorry." (미안해요.). When to use it: 실수했을 때 사과해요. Note: 더 미안할 때: I’m really sorry.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "That’s okay.".

Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Ben helps Jiwoo.
2. The box is light.
3. Ben is fine.
The scene they are about:
1. Ben: "Hi! I’m Ben. Can I help?" (안녕하세요! 저는 벤이에요. 도와 드릴까요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Yes, please. Thank you so much. I’m Jiwoo." (네, 부탁해요. 정말 고마워요. 저는 지우예요.)
3. Ben: "No problem, Jiwoo. Wow, it’s heavy!" (별거 아니에요, 지우 씨. 와, 무겁네요!)
4. Jiwoo: "Oops! I’m sorry! Your foot!" (앗! 미안해요! 발!)
5. Ben: "That’s okay. I’m fine." (괜찮아요. 저 멀쩡해요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Are you sure?" (정말요?)
7. Ben: "Yes! No worries." (네! 걱정 마요.)
8. Jiwoo: "Ben, you’re a great neighbor." (벤, 정말 좋은 이웃이에요.)
9. Ben: "Aw, thanks. Welcome to the building!" (아이, 고마워요. 우리 건물에 온 걸 환영해요!)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: Thank you so much. — You’re welcome.
head: 이럴 때
말하기
대답하기
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Thank you so much. — You’re welcome. / I’m sorry. — That’s okay. Table (이럴 때 → 말하기):
- 도움을 받았을 때 → Thank you so much.
- 실수했을 때 → I’m sorry.
- 지나가야 할 때 → Excuse me.
- 아주 미안할 때 → I’m really sorry.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
Thank you *so much*. 정말 고마워요.
I’m *really* sorry. 정말 미안해요.

먼저 양해를 구할 땐 Excuse me.
이미 실수했으면 Sorry.
errors: 늦어서 미안할 땐 I’m sorry I’m late.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- so · really로 마음 더하기: Thank you so much. 정말 고마워요. / I’m really sorry. 정말 미안해요.
- Excuse me · Sorry: 먼저 양해를 구할 땐 Excuse me. / 이미 실수했으면 Sorry.
Common mistakes on screen:
- I’m sorry for you. → I’m sorry. (sorry for you는 ‘안됐다’는 뜻이에요.)
- Thank you so. → Thank you so much. (so 뒤에 much를 붙여요.)
- I’m sorry for late. → I’m sorry I’m late. (늦어서 미안할 땐 I’m sorry I’m late.)
- Excuse me! (발을 밟은 뒤) → I’m sorry! (이미 실수했으면 sorry.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

Thank you so. → Thank you so much.
I’m sorry for late. → I’m sorry I’m late.

steps.note: 선생님이 상황을 말하면 알맞은 말로 대답해요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 선생님이 상황을 말하면 알맞은 말로 대답해요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: 도움을 받았어요 → Thank you so much. | 늦었어요 → I’m sorry I’m late. | 선물을 받았어요 → Thanks for the gift! | 내가 틀렸어요 → Sorry, my mistake.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Thank you so much!" (고마워요, 미안해요); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Thank you so much." / "I’m sorry." / "That’s okay.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 고마움: "Thanks a lot." (정말 고마워요., 친근); "You’re welcome." (천만에요., 보통)
- 사과: "Sorry, my mistake." (미안해요, 제 실수예요., 보통); "I’m really sorry." (정말 미안해요., 보통); "Excuse me." (실례합니다., 정중)
- 괜찮다고 할 때: "No worries." (괜찮아요., 친근); "It’s not your fault." (당신 잘못 아니에요., 보통); "Don’t worry." (걱정 마요., 보통); "It’s all right." (괜찮아요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 고마움·미안함의 몸짓

steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 고마움·미안함의 몸짓: 감사·사과의 몸짓은 사람과 상황에 따라 달라요. bow(고개 숙이기) · handshake(악수) · hug(포옹) / 악수나 포옹은 상대가 편안해할 때만 해요.
- Oops!: 작은 실수를 했을 때 바로 나오는 말이에요. ‘앗!’ / Oops! Sorry!
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Thank you so ___. B: You’re ___. / A: Oops! I’m ___. B: That’s ___. / 낱말 상자: much · welcome · sorry · okay
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: thank you (고마워요), sorry (미안해요), gift (선물), hug (포옹), bow (고개 숙여 인사), handshake (악수), oops (앗!), mistake (실수), worry (걱정하다), excuse me (실례합니다), help (돕다), late (늦은).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: fault (잘못) — "It’s not your fault."; problem (문제) — "No problem."; pardon (뭐라고요?) — "Pardon?"; all right (괜찮은) — "It’s all right."; heavy (무거운) — "It’s heavy!"; sure (확실한) — "Are you sure?"; need (필요하다) — "Need a hand?"; hand (손; 도움) — "give me a hand 도와주다"; kind (친절한) — "You’re so kind.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: Someone helps you. What do you say?
You’re late. What do you say?
Someone says, “I’m sorry.” What do you say?

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Someone helps you. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Thank you so much.)
- "You’re late. What do you say?" (hint on screen: I’m sorry I’m late.)
- "Someone says, “I’m sorry.” What do you say?" (hint on screen: That’s okay. / No worries.)
- "Say thank you to someone in your life." (hint on screen: Thank you, ___, for ___.)
- "I say, “Thank you!” What do you say?" (hint on screen: You’re welcome.)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: Good Neighbors
steps.text: Moving is hard. It’s Saturday, and Jiwoo still has many boxes. Her neighbor Ben helps her. Oops! A box falls on his foot. Jiwoo says, “I’m sorry!” Ben says, “That’s okay. No worries.” Then Grace gives her some cookies. Jiwoo says, “Thank you so much!” She has *such* good neighbors.
steps.gloss: move 이사하다 · still 아직 · fall 떨어지다 · foot 발 · cookie 쿠키 · such 정말 그런
questions: Who helps Jiwoo with the boxes?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Good Neighbors". Text: "Moving is hard. It’s Saturday, and Jiwoo still has many boxes. Her neighbor Ben helps her. Oops! A box falls on his foot. Jiwoo says, “I’m sorry!” Ben says, “That’s okay. No worries.” Then Grace gives her some cookies. Jiwoo says, “Thank you so much!” She has such good neighbors." Words: move 이사하다 · still 아직 · fall 떨어지다 · foot 발 · cookie 쿠키 · such 정말 그런.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Who helps Jiwoo with the boxes?" / "What does Grace give her?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Thank you so much.’로 마음을 담아 고마워할 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Thank you so much.’로 마음을 담아 고마워할 수 있어요.
- ‘I’m sorry.’로 사과할 수 있어요.
- ‘That’s okay.’ / ‘You’re welcome.’으로 대답할 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

steps.title: 새 이웃
steps.scene_desc: 아침, 아파트 모퉁이의 작은 카페. 창가 자리의 대니얼(책과 노트북)과 커피를 받아 든 지우가 인사
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Where are you from?" (새 이웃). Goal: 어디에서 왔는지 묻고 답하기. Today's scene: 아침, 아파트 모퉁이의 작은 카페. 창가 자리의 대니얼(책과 노트북)과 커피를 받아 든 지우가 인사. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Where are you from?".

steps.when: 처음 만난 사람에게 고향이나 나라를 물을 때 써요.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Where are you from?" (어디에서 왔어요?). When to use it: 처음 만난 사람에게 고향이나 나라를 물을 때 써요. Note: Where = 어디, from = ~에서.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I’m from ___.".

steps.when: 내 나라나 도시를 말할 때 써요.
steps.extra: I’m from Korea. · I’m from Busan.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I’m from ___." (~에서 왔어요.). When to use it: 내 나라나 도시를 말할 때 써요. Note: I’m from Korea. · I’m from Busan.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Nice to meet you.".

steps.extra: 대답: Nice to meet you, too.
steps.teach:
Expression 3 of 3: "Nice to meet you." (만나서 반가워요.). When to use it: 처음 인사할 때 써요. Note: 대답: Nice to meet you, too.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("At the Café · 아침, 동네 카페에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: At the Café · 아침, 동네 카페에서

lines.en: Hi, Daniel. I’m Jiwoo. I live near here.
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 대니얼. 지우예요. 이 근처에 살아요.

lines.en: Nice to meet you, too. {{Where are you from}}?
{{I’m from}} the United States. From Chicago.

steps.teach:

1. Daniel: "Good morning! I’m Daniel." (좋은 아침이에요! 저는 대니얼이에요.)
2. Jiwoo: "Hi, Daniel. I’m Jiwoo. I live near here." (안녕하세요, 대니얼. 지우예요. 이 근처에 살아요.)
3. Daniel: "Nice to meet you, Jiwoo." (만나서 반가워요, 지우.)
4. Jiwoo: "Nice to meet you, too. Where are you from?" (저도 반가워요. 어디에서 왔어요?)
5. Daniel: "I’m from the United States. From Chicago." (미국에서 왔어요. 시카고요.)
6. Daniel: "And you? Are you from Seoul?" (지우는요? 서울 사람이에요?)
7. Jiwoo: "No, I’m from Busan." (아니요, 부산에서 왔어요.)
8. Daniel: "Busan! Why Seoul?" (부산이요! 왜 서울에 왔어요?)
9. Jiwoo: "For my new job." (새 직장 때문에요.)
10. Daniel: "Oh, I see! Welcome to the neighborhood." (아, 그렇군요! 동네에 온 걸 환영해요.)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.

10. Daniel: "Oh, I see! Welcome to the neighborhood." (아, 그렇군요! 동네에 온 걸 환영해요.)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: 어디
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Where are you from? / I’m from ___. Table (어디 → 이렇게 말해요):
- Korea 한국 → I’m from Korea.
- Busan 부산 → I’m from Busan.
- the United States 미국 → I’m from the United States.
- Canada 캐나다 → I’m from Canada.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
‘저는 ~예요’는 I am. 말할 땐 줄여서 I’m.
*I’m* from Korea.
*You’re* from Chicago. (You’re = You are)

나라·도시 이름은 대문자로 시작해요: Korea, Canada.
‘the’가 붙는 나라: *the* United States, *the* UK
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- I’m = I am: ‘저는 ~예요’는 I am. 말할 땐 줄여서 I’m. / I’m from Korea. / You’re from Chicago. (You’re = You are)
- from + 나라·도시: 나라·도시 이름은 대문자로 시작해요: Korea, Canada. / ‘the’가 붙는 나라: the United States, the UK
Common mistakes on screen:
- I from Korea. → I’m from Korea. (am(’m)을 빼지 않아요.)
- I’m Korea. → I’m from Korea. (‘~에서 왔어요’는 from. ‘I’m Korean.’(한국 사람이에요)도 맞아요.)
- Where you are from? → Where are you from? (물을 땐 are가 앞으로 와요.)
- I’m from United States. → I’m from the United States. (the를 붙이는 나라예요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) Toronto / Canada → I’m from Toronto, Canada. · 도시, 나라 순서로 말해요.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) Toronto / Canada → I’m from Toronto, Canada. · 도시, 나라 순서로 말해요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: Toronto → Canada | Chicago → the United States | Seoul → Korea | Osaka → Japan.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Where are you from?" (새 이웃); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Where are you from?" / "I’m from ___." / "Nice to meet you.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 사는 곳: "I live in ___." (~에 살아요., 보통); "I’m your new neighbor." (새로 온 이웃이에요., 보통); "Which floor are you on?" (몇 층에 살아요?, 친근); "I’m on the ___ floor." (~층에 살아요., 보통)

- 맞장구: "Oh, really?" (아, 정말요?, 친근); "That’s great." (좋네요., 보통); "Me, too." (저도요., 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:
Word list on screen: live (살다) — "I live near here."; next (옆의, 다음의) — "next door 옆집"; really (정말) — "Oh, really?"; great (아주 좋은) — "That’s great."; state (주(州)) — "the United States 미국(여러 주가 모인 나라)"; from (~에서) — "I’m from Busan."; where (어디) — "Where are you from?"; near (가까이) — "near here 이 근처"; neighborhood (동네) — "Welcome to the neighborhood.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "Where are you from?" (hint on screen: I’m from ___.)
- "Are you from a big city?" (hint on screen: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.)
- "Say hello to a new neighbor!" (hint on screen: Hi, I’m ___. Nice to meet you.)

Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.

steps.title: 천천히 말해 주세요
steps.goal: 못 알아들었을 때 다시·천천히 말해 달라고 하기
steps.scene_desc: 아파트 엘리베이터 안. 머스터드색 니트의 벤이 신나게 빠르게 말하고, 지우는 당황한 얼굴로 손을 살짝 듦
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can you speak slowly?" (천천히 말해 주세요). Goal: 못 알아들었을 때 다시·천천히 말해 달라고 하기. Today's scene: 아파트 엘리베이터 안. 머스터드색 니트의 벤이 신나게 빠르게 말하고, 지우는 당황한 얼굴로 손을 살짝 듦. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Sorry, I don’t understand.".

steps.extra: 못 알아들어도 괜찮아요. 이렇게 말하면 돼요.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Sorry, I don’t understand." (죄송해요, 못 알아들었어요.). When to use it: 말을 이해하지 못했을 때 써요. Note: 못 알아들어도 괜찮아요. 이렇게 말하면 돼요.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Can you speak slowly, please?".

Expression 2 of 3: "Can you speak slowly, please?" (천천히 말해 줄래요?). When to use it: 말이 너무 빠를 때 부탁해요. Note: please를 붙이면 더 부드러워요.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "What does ___ mean?".

Expression 3 of 3: "What does ___ mean?" (~가 무슨 뜻이에요?). When to use it: 모르는 낱말의 뜻을 물어요. Note: What does “need” mean?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("In the Elevator · 엘리베이터에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: In the Elevator · 엘리베이터에서

lines.en: Hey, Jiwoo! How’s the new place? All settled in? Need any help with anything?
lines.ko: 안녕하세요, 지우 씨! 새집은 어때요? 짐 정리는 다 했어요? 뭐 도와줄 거 있어요?

lines.en: Sorry, {{I don’t understand}}. {{Can you speak slowly, please}}?
lines.ko: 미안해요, 못 알아들었어요. 천천히 말해 줄 수 있어요?

Great. I’m on the third floor. Need help?
It means “필요하다.” Do you need help?

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "In the Elevator · 엘리베이터에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

2. Jiwoo: "Sorry, I don’t understand. Can you speak slowly, please?" (미안해요, 못 알아들었어요. 천천히 말해 줄 수 있어요?)
3. Ben: "Oh! No worries. Is… your… new… home… okay?" (아! 괜찮아요. 새… 집은… 괜찮아요?)
4. Jiwoo: "Yes, it’s good. Thanks, Ben." (네, 좋아요. 고마워요, 벤.)
5. Ben: "Great. I’m on the third floor. Need help?" (잘됐네요. 저는 3층에 있어요. 도움 필요해요?)
6. Jiwoo: "“Need”? What does “need” mean?" (“Need”요? “need”가 무슨 뜻이에요?)
7. Ben: "It means “필요하다.” Do you need help?" (“필요하다”라는 뜻이에요. 도움이 필요해요?)
8. Jiwoo: "Oh! No, thanks. I’m okay." (아! 아니요, 고마워요. 괜찮아요.)
9. Ben: "Got it. See you around!" (알겠어요. 또 봐요!)

rows: 한 번 더 듣고 싶을 때
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Can you speak slowly, please? / What does ___ mean? — It means ___. Table (이럴 때 → 이렇게 말해요):
- 못 알아들었을 때 → Sorry, I don’t understand.
- 너무 빠를 때 → Can you speak slowly, please?
- 한 번 더 듣고 싶을 때 → One more time, please.
- 뜻을 모를 때 → What does “need” mean?
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
I understand.를 부정하면 I *don’t* understand.
여기서 don’t는 ‘이해하지 못한다’는 뜻을 만들어요.

부탁할 때 써요.
*Can you* speak slowly, *please*?
*Can you* write it down?
errors: I understand의 부정은 no가 아니라 동사 앞에 don’t.
Sorry, I don’t know. (못 알아들었을 때)
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- don’t + 동사: I understand.를 부정하면 I don’t understand. / 여기서 don’t는 ‘이해하지 못한다’는 뜻을 만들어요.
- Can you ~, please?: 부탁할 때 써요. / Can you speak slowly, please? / Can you write it down?
Common mistakes on screen:
- I no understand. → I don’t understand. (I understand의 부정은 no가 아니라 동사 앞에 don’t.)
- What mean “need”? → What does “need” mean? (does를 넣고 mean은 끝에.)
- Sorry, I don’t know. (못 알아들었을 때) → Sorry, I don’t understand. (know는 ‘알다’, understand는 ‘이해하다’.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.
points: don’t + 동사: I understand.를 부정하면 I don’t understand.여기서 don’t는 ‘이해하지 못한다’는 뜻을 만들어요.

mistakes: I no understand. → I don’t understand.
What mean “need”? → What does “need” mean?
Sorry, I don’t know. (못 알아들었을 때) → Sorry, I don’t understand.

steps.note: 예) busy → What does “busy” mean? — It means 바쁜.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) busy → What does “busy” mean? — It means 바쁜. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: busy → 바쁜? | neighbor → 이웃? | floor → 층? | welcome → 환영?
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Can you speak slowly?" (천천히 말해 주세요); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Sorry, I don’t understand." / "Can you speak slowly, please?" / "What does ___ mean?". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: How do you say ___ in English?
steps.teach:
More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 다시 듣기: "Sorry?" (네?(못 들었을 때), 친근); "Pardon?" (뭐라고 하셨죠?, 정중); "One more time, please." (한 번만 더요., 보통)
- 말·뜻 묻기: "How do you say ___ in English?" (~를 영어로 어떻게 말해요?, 보통); "Can you write it down?" (적어 줄 수 있어요?, 보통); "Is this right?" (이거 맞아요?, 보통)
- 알아들었을 때: "I see." (아, 그렇군요., 보통); "I got it." (알겠어요., 친근); "Let me think." (생각 좀 해 볼게요., 보통)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

boxes: 못 알아들어도 괜찮아요

원어민끼리도 자주 다시 물어요. Sorry?를 끝을 올려(↗) 말하면 ‘뭐라고요?’가 돼요.
메모: Can you slowly speak?도 가능해요. 이 상황에서는 Can you speak slowly, please?가 더 자연스러워요.
information 정보

안내 데스크는 Information.
Where is the information desk? 안내 데스크가 어디예요?
steps.blank:
A: Sorry, I don’t ___. Can you speak ___, please?
B: Sure.   A: What ___ “floor” mean?
낱말 상자: understand · slowly · does
steps.teach:
Tips on screen:
- 못 알아들어도 괜찮아요: 원어민끼리도 자주 다시 물어요. Sorry?를 끝을 올려(↗) 말하면 ‘뭐라고요?’가 돼요. / 메모: Can you slowly speak?도 가능해요. 이 상황에서는 Can you speak slowly, please?가 더 자연스러워요.
- information 정보: 안내 데스크는 Information. / Where is the information desk? 안내 데스크가 어디예요?
Fill-in-the-blank dialogue on screen: A: Sorry, I don’t ___. Can you speak ___, please? / B: Sure. A: What ___ “floor” mean? / 낱말 상자: understand · slowly · does
Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: speak (말하다), listen (듣다), write (쓰다), understand (이해하다), question (질문), answer (대답), word (낱말), English (영어), Korean (한국어), slowly (천천히), information (정보, 안내). Review words: help (돕다, 도움).
Go through about six, new ones first: call highlight_word with the word, say it, and let the learner say it. Now and then ask a tiny real question with the word (for example: Are you a morning person?) and react to the answer. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a word list.

Word list on screen: mean (뜻하다) — "What does it mean?"; say (말하다) — "How do you say it?"; down (아래로) — "write it down 적다"; right (맞는) — "Is this right?"; wrong (틀린) — "It’s wrong."; know (알다) — "I don’t know."; need (필요하다) — "Do you need help?"; please (~해 주세요) — "Slowly, please."; fast (빠르게) — "He speaks fast.".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): questions about the learner's own life.

items: How do you say “안녕하세요” in English?
Yes, a little. / No, it’s okay.
I’m speaking too fast. What do you say?
Ask me what a word means.
steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "How do you say “안녕하세요” in English?" (hint on screen: You say “Hello.”)
- "What does “neighbor” mean?" (hint on screen: It means 이웃.)
- "Is English hard for you?" (hint on screen: Yes, a little. / No, it’s okay.)
- "I’m speaking too fast. What do you say?" (hint on screen: Can you speak slowly, please?)
- "Ask me what a word means." (hint on screen: What does ___ mean?)
Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
questions: How do you say “안녕하세요” in English?
I’m speaking too fast. What do you say?
Ask me what a word means.

steps.title: Ben Talks Fast
steps.text: Ben is from Boston. He lives on the third floor. He talks fast! Jiwoo says, “Can you speak slowly, please?” Ben smiles and says, “Of course.” Now he speaks slowly. He is a good neighbor.
steps.gloss: fast 빨리 · smile 미소 짓다 · now 이제 · slowly 천천히
questions: What floor does Ben live on?
steps.teach:
Reading on screen: "Ben Talks Fast". Text: "Ben is from Boston. He lives on the third floor. He talks fast! Jiwoo says, “Can you speak slowly, please?” Ben smiles and says, “Of course.” Now he speaks slowly. He is a good neighbor." Words: fast 빨리 · smile 미소 짓다 · now 이제 · slowly 천천히.
Read the text aloud exactly as written at a natural pace, then ask the questions one at a time: "Where is Ben from?" / "What floor does Ben live on?". React to their answers; if one is not right, point to the sentence. You may add one short personal question linked to the reading. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the 'I can' check-out.

items: ‘Sorry, I don’t understand.’로 못 알아들었다고 말할 수 있어요.
‘Can you speak slowly, please?’로 천천히 말해 달라고 할 수 있어요.
‘What does ___ mean?’으로 뜻을 물을 수 있어요.
steps.teach:
Check-out. The 'I can' list on screen:
- ‘Sorry, I don’t understand.’로 못 알아들었다고 말할 수 있어요.
- ‘Can you speak slowly, please?’로 천천히 말해 달라고 할 수 있어요.
- ‘What does ___ mean?’으로 뜻을 물을 수 있어요.
Ask the learner to pick one and show it by saying a sentence; react and praise specifically. Then end like a person: ask how this lesson felt, react, say that the next lesson comes next, and say a warm goodbye. Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

lessons.title: 카페에서 주문
lessons.title_en: Can I have a coffee, please?
lessons.goal: 원하는 것을 공손하게 달라고 하고 고맙다고 말하기

steps.title: 카페에서 주문
steps.title_en: Can I have a coffee, please?
steps.goal: 원하는 것을 공손하게 달라고 하고 고맙다고 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 동네 모퉁이 카페 계산대. 지우가 주문하고, 옆에서 대니얼이 진열장의 치즈케이크를 가리킴. 직원이 컵을 건넴
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can I have a coffee, please?" (카페에서 주문). Goal: 원하는 것을 공손하게 달라고 하고 고맙다고 말하기. Today's scene: 동네 모퉁이 카페 계산대. 지우가 주문하고, 옆에서 대니얼이 진열장의 치즈케이크를 가리킴. 직원이 컵을 건넴. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Can I have ___, please?".

steps.extra: Can I have a latte, please?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Can I have ___, please?" (~ 주시겠어요?). When to use it: 카페·가게에서 공손하게 달라고 해요. Note: Can I have a latte, please?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Here you are.".

Expression 2 of 3: "Here you are." (여기 있어요.). When to use it: 물건을 건네줄 때 써요. Note: = Here it is.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Thank you!".

Expression 3 of 3: "Thank you!" (고마워요!). When to use it: 받고 나서 인사해요. Note: 짧게: Thanks!
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Cheesecake · 동네 카페 계산대에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Cheesecake · 동네 카페 계산대에서

lines.en: Hi! What can I get you?
Hi, Jiwoo! Try the cheesecake. It’s great.
lines.ko: 안녕, 지우! 치즈케이크 먹어 봐요. 맛있어요.

lines.en: Good question. The cream is so fresh!
Okay! {{Can I have}} a slice of cheesecake, too?

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Cheesecake · 동네 카페 계산대에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Staff: "Hi! What can I get you?" (안녕하세요! 뭐 드릴까요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Can I have an iced latte, please?" (아이스 라테 주시겠어요?)
3. Staff: "Sure. Small or large?" (네. 작은 거요, 큰 거요?)
4. Jiwoo: "Small, please." (작은 걸로요.)
5. Daniel: "Hi, Jiwoo! Try the cheesecake. It’s great." (안녕, 지우! 치즈케이크 먹어 봐요. 맛있어요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Why?" (왜요?)
7. Daniel: "Good question. The cream is so fresh!" (좋은 질문이에요. 크림이 정말 신선하거든요!)
8. Jiwoo: "Okay! Can I have a slice of cheesecake, too?" (좋아요! 치즈케이크도 한 조각 주시겠어요?)
9. Staff: "Here you are." (여기 있어요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Thank you!" (고맙습니다!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.title: Cheesecake · 동네 카페 계산대에서

lines.en: Hi! What can I get you?
Hi, Jiwoo! Try the cheesecake. It’s great.

Okay! {{Can I have}} a slice of cheesecake, too?

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Staff, Daniel exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Staff (you): "Hi! What can I get you?" (안녕하세요! 뭐 드릴까요?)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "Can I have an iced latte, please?" (아이스 라테 주시겠어요?)
3. Staff (you): "Sure. Small or large?" (네. 작은 거요, 큰 거요?)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "Small, please." (작은 걸로요.)
5. Daniel (you): "Hi, Jiwoo! Try the cheesecake. It’s great." (안녕, 지우! 치즈케이크 먹어 봐요. 맛있어요.)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Why?" (왜요?)
7. Daniel (you): "Good question. The cream is so fresh!" (좋은 질문이에요. 크림이 정말 신선하거든요!)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "Okay! Can I have a slice of cheesecake, too?" (좋아요! 치즈케이크도 한 조각 주시겠어요?)
9. Staff (you): "Here you are." (여기 있어요.)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "Thank you!" (고맙습니다!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Staff and Daniel. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. Jiwoo gets a large latte.
2. Daniel likes the cheesecake.
3. The cream is fresh.
The scene they are about:
1. Staff: "Hi! What can I get you?" (안녕하세요! 뭐 드릴까요?)
2. Jiwoo: "Can I have an iced latte, please?" (아이스 라테 주시겠어요?)
3. Staff: "Sure. Small or large?" (네. 작은 거요, 큰 거요?)
4. Jiwoo: "Small, please." (작은 걸로요.)
5. Daniel: "Hi, Jiwoo! Try the cheesecake. It’s great." (안녕, 지우! 치즈케이크 먹어 봐요. 맛있어요.)
6. Jiwoo: "Why?" (왜요?)
7. Daniel: "Good question. The cream is so fresh!" (좋은 질문이에요. 크림이 정말 신선하거든요!)
8. Jiwoo: "Okay! Can I have a slice of cheesecake, too?" (좋아요! 치즈케이크도 한 조각 주시겠어요?)
9. Staff: "Here you are." (여기 있어요.)
10. Jiwoo: "Thank you!" (고맙습니다!)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: 무엇을
이렇게 말해요
rows: Can I have a coffee, please?
Can I have an iced tea, please?
Can I have a cookie, please?
Can I have some water, please?
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Can I have ___, please? / Here you are. — Thank you! Table (무엇을 → 이렇게 말해요):
- a coffee 커피 한 잔 → Can I have a coffee, please?
- an iced tea 아이스티 → Can I have an iced tea, please?
- a cookie 쿠키 → Can I have a cookie, please?
- some water 물 좀 → Can I have some water, please?
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
공손하게 주문하는 말이에요.
끝에 *please*를 붙이면 더 부드러워요.
Can I have a tea, *please*?

*a* coffee 커피 한 잔(하나)
*some* water 물 좀 — 기본은 some
한 잔을 분명히: *a glass of* water
errors: Can I have a coffee, please?
명령처럼 들려요. Can I have로 부탁해요.
Can I 뒤에는 have 그대로 써요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- Can I have ~, please?: 공손하게 주문하는 말이에요. / 끝에 please를 붙이면 더 부드러워요. / Can I have a tea, please?
- a / some: a coffee 커피 한 잔(하나) / some water 물 좀 — 기본은 some / 한 잔을 분명히: a glass of water
Common mistakes on screen:
- Give me coffee. → Can I have a coffee, please? (명령처럼 들려요. Can I have로 부탁해요.)
- Can I has a coffee? → Can I have a coffee? (Can I 뒤에는 have 그대로 써요.)
- Here are you. → Here you are. (순서를 바꾸지 않아요.)
- Thank. → Thank you! / Thanks! (Thank 혼자는 쓰지 않아요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.

steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). 2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s this?" (이건 뭐예요?). Goal: 물건 이름과 색을 묻고 말하기. Today's scene: 지우와 클로이의 사무실 책상. 클로이가 분홍 열쇠고리를 들어 보이고, 클로이 책상은 알록달록, 지우 책상은 흑백.
