steps.title: 전화번호
steps.scene_desc: 점심, 회사 근처 식당. 클로이가 친구 마야(세이지 블라우스)를 지우에게 소개하고, 마야가 휴대폰을 꺼내 번호를 받는 모습
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What’s your phone number?" (전화번호). Goal: 숫자로 전화번호를 묻고 말하고, 확인하기. Today's scene: 점심, 회사 근처 식당. 클로이가 친구 마야(세이지 블라우스)를 지우에게 소개하고, 마야가 휴대폰을 꺼내 번호를 받는 모습. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What’s your phone number?".

Expression 1 of 3: "What’s your phone number?" (전화번호가 뭐예요?). When to use it: 연락처를 물을 때 써요. Note: 짧게: What’s your number?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It’s ___.".

Expression 2 of 3: "It’s ___." (~예요.). When to use it: 번호를 말할 때 써요. Note: It’s 555-0123.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Can you say that again?".

The app has just played this scene, "Lunch with Maya · 점심, 회사 근처 식당에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

head: 숫자
읽는 법
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What’s your phone number? / It’s ___. Table (숫자 → 읽는 법):
- 0 (전화번호 속) → oh (보통) · zero
- 11 ~ 19 → eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen … nineteen
- 60 · 70 · 80 · 90 → sixty · seventy · eighty · ninety
- 555-0139 → five-five-five, oh-one-three-nine
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
0139 → oh-one-three-nine
0은 보통 oh라고 읽어요. 같은 숫자 둘은 double: 55 → double five.

thirteen(13) ↔ thirty(30)
-teen은 뒤를 세게: thir-*TEEN*
-ty는 앞을 세게: *THIR*-ty
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 전화번호는 한 자리씩: 0139 → oh-one-three-nine / 0은 보통 oh라고 읽어요. 같은 숫자 둘은 double: 55 → double five.
- -teen 과 -ty: thirteen(13) ↔ thirty(30) / -teen은 뒤를 세게: thir-TEEN / -ty는 앞을 세게: THIR-ty
Common mistakes on screen:
- What is your phone? → What’s your phone number? (phone은 ‘전화기’예요. number를 붙여요.)
- Can you again? → Can you say that again? (say that을 꼭 넣어요.)
- one hundred thirty-nine… → oh-one-three-nine (전화번호는 한 자리씩 읽어요.)
- fifty (15를 말할 때) → fifteen (-teen은 뒤를 세게: fif-TEEN.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 두 숫자를 번갈아 말해요: thirteen — thirty. 선생님이 하나를 말하면 어느 쪽인지 맞혀 봐요. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: 13 → 30 | 14 → 40 | 15 → 50 | 19 → 90.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "What’s your phone number?" (전화번호); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.

head: 지금 상태
같이 하자고 하기
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: I’m hungry. / I’m thirsty. / Let’s ___. Table (지금 상태 → 같이 하자고 하기):
- hungry 배고픈 → Let’s eat.

items:
*I’m* hungry. *I’m* thirsty. *I’m* full.
‘배가 고프다’도 영어에서는 ‘나는 배고픈 상태예요’라고 말해요.

같이 하자는 말이에요.
*Let’s* eat. *Let’s* go.
-ing를 붙이지 않아요.

steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- I’m + 상태: I’m hungry. I’m thirsty. I’m full. / ‘배가 고프다’도 영어에서는 ‘나는 배고픈 상태예요’라고 말해요.
- Let’s + 동사: 같이 하자는 말이에요. / Let’s eat. Let’s go. / -ing를 붙이지 않아요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- I hungry. → I’m hungry. (’m을 빼지 않아요.)
- Let’s eating. → Let’s eat. (Let’s 뒤엔 동사 그대로.)
- I want eat pizza. → I want to eat pizza. / I want pizza. (want 뒤에 동사가 오면 to.)
- I’m full stomach. → I’m full. (full 하나로 ‘배불러요’.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.

steps.teach:

- Do you like ~?: Do you like fish? — Yes, I do. / No, I don’t. / 짧게 대답할 땐 like를 다시 안 써요.

steps.title: 얼마예요?
steps.goal: 값을 묻고 카드로 낼 수 있는지 묻기
steps.scene_desc: 저녁, 아파트 앞 편의점 계산대. 지우가 과자를 들고 카드를 내밀고, 옆에서 그레이스가 미소 지으며 지켜봄. 직원이 영수증을 건넴
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "How much is it?" (얼마예요?). Goal: 값을 묻고 카드로 낼 수 있는지 묻기. Today's scene: 저녁, 아파트 앞 편의점 계산대. 지우가 과자를 들고 카드를 내밀고, 옆에서 그레이스가 미소 지으며 지켜봄. 직원이 영수증을 건넴. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "How much is it?".

Expression 1 of 3: "How much is it?" (얼마예요?). When to use it: 가격을 물어요. Note: 여럿이면 How much are they?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It’s ___ dollars.".

Expression 2 of 3: "It’s ___ dollars." (~달러예요.). When to use it: 가격을 말해요. 한국 돈은 won. Note: It’s three dollars. · It’s 4,500 won.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Can I pay by card?".

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What time is it now?" (hint on screen: It’s ___.)
- "What time do you eat lunch?" (hint on screen: I eat lunch at ___.)
- "Are you early or late today?" (hint on screen: I’m early. / I’m a little late.)

Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.

steps.title: 우리 가족
steps.goal: 사진 속 가족을 소개하고 식구 수를 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 그레이스의 거실. 그레이스가 가족사진 액자를 보여 주고, 지우가 들여다보는 모습. 소파 위에 고양이 모찌
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Who’s this?" (우리 가족). Goal: 사진 속 가족을 소개하고 식구 수를 말하기. Today's scene: 그레이스의 거실. 그레이스가 가족사진 액자를 보여 주고, 지우가 들여다보는 모습. 소파 위에 고양이 모찌. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Who’s this?".

steps.when: 사진 속 사람이나 옆 사람이 누구인지 물어요.
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "Who’s this?" (이 사람은 누구예요?). When to use it: 사진 속 사람이나 옆 사람이 누구인지 물어요. Note: Who’s = Who is.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "This is my ___.".

steps.extra: This is my mom. · This is my friend, Ben.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "This is my ___." (제 ~예요.). When to use it: 가족이나 친구를 소개해요. Note: This is my mom. · This is my friend, Ben.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "I have two ___s.".

Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("Grace’s Family · 그레이스의 거실에서") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

steps.title: Grace’s Family · 그레이스의 거실에서

lines.en: Come in, Jiwoo. Look! My family.
{{This is my}} mom. And this is my dad.

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Grace’s Family · 그레이스의 거실에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

4. Jiwoo: "And this woman?" (그럼 이 여자분은요?)
5. Grace: "This is my aunt. She has twins!" (우리 이모예요. 쌍둥이가 있어요!)
6. Jiwoo: "Wow! I have two brothers." (와! 저는 남자 형제가 둘 있어요.)
7. Jiwoo: "And who’s this man?" (그럼 이 남자분은요?)

9. Jiwoo: "So cute!" (정말 귀여워요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

4. Jiwoo (learner): "And this woman?" (그럼 이 여자분은요?)
5. Grace (you): "This is my aunt. She has twins!" (우리 이모예요. 쌍둥이가 있어요!)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Wow! I have two brothers." (와! 저는 남자 형제가 둘 있어요.)
7. Jiwoo (learner): "And who’s this man?" (그럼 이 남자분은요?)

9. Jiwoo (learner): "So cute!" (정말 귀여워요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Grace. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

items: The woman Jiwoo asks about is Grace’s aunt.
steps.teach:
True/false check. The statements on the learner's screen:
1. The woman Jiwoo asks about is Grace’s aunt.
2. Jiwoo has two sisters.
3. Mochi is a cat.

2. Jiwoo: "Who’s this?" (이분은 누구예요?)

5. Grace: "This is my aunt. She has twins!" (우리 이모예요. 쌍둥이가 있어요!)
6. Jiwoo: "Wow! I have two brothers." (와! 저는 남자 형제가 둘 있어요.)
7. Jiwoo: "And who’s this man?" (그럼 이 남자분은요?)

9. Jiwoo: "So cute!" (정말 귀여워요!)
Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

head: 가족
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Who’s this? / This is my ___. Table (가족 → 이렇게 말해요):
- mom 엄마 → This is my mom.
- dad 아빠 → This is my dad.
- brother 형제 → I have two brothers.
- sister 자매 → I have a sister.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
사람을 가리키며 소개해요.
*This is* my mom. 이분은 우리 엄마예요.
조금 떨어져 있으면 *That’s* my uncle.

one brother → two brother*s*
one sister → three sister*s*
특별한 낱말: child → children
errors: This is my mother of me.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- This is ~: 사람을 가리키며 소개해요. / This is my mom. 이분은 우리 엄마예요. / 조금 떨어져 있으면 That’s my uncle.
- 둘 이상이면 -s: one brother → two brothers / one sister → three sisters / 특별한 낱말: child → children
Common mistakes on screen:
- I have two brother. → I have two brothers. (둘 이상이면 -s.)
- He is my aunt. → She is my aunt. (aunt(이모·고모)는 여자라서 she.)
- I have two childs. → I have two children. (child의 여럿은 children.)
- This is my mother of me. → This is my mother. (my 하나면 충분해요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) cousin / 3 → I have three cousins. · 1이면 I have a brother.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) cousin / 3 → I have three cousins. · 1이면 I have a brother. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: sister → 2 | brother → 1 | cousin → 3 | uncle → 2.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "Who’s this?" (우리 가족); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "Who’s this?" / "This is my ___." / "I have two ___s.". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

groups: How many people are in your family?
steps.teach:

steps.title: 어디 있어요?
steps.goal: 물건이 어디 있는지 묻고 위치(on·under)를 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 벤의 집 현관 앞. 벤이 소파 쿠션을 들추며 열쇠를 찾고, 지우가 웃으며 벤의 바지 주머니를 가리킴
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Where is my key?" (어디 있어요?). Goal: 물건이 어디 있는지 묻고 위치(on·under)를 말하기. Today's scene: 벤의 집 현관 앞. 벤이 소파 쿠션을 들추며 열쇠를 찾고, 지우가 웃으며 벤의 바지 주머니를 가리킴. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Where is my ___?".

Expression 1 of 3: "Where is my ___?" (제 ~ 어디 있어요?). When to use it: 물건이 어디 있는지 물어요. Note: Where is my phone?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "It’s on / under the ___.".

Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.

steps.title: Ben’s Key · 벤의 거실에서

lines.en: Ben… look! It’s in your pocket!

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "Ben’s Key · 벤의 거실에서", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:
1. Ben: "Oh no. Where is my key?" (아이고. 내 열쇠 어디 있지?)
2. Jiwoo: "Is it on the table?" (탁자 위에 있어요?)
3. Ben: "No." (아니요.)
4. Jiwoo: "Is it under the sofa?" (소파 밑에는요?)
5. Ben: "No…" (아니요…)
6. Jiwoo: "Is it on the shelf?" (선반 위는요?)
7. Ben: "No! Where is it?" (아니요! 어디 있는 거지?)
8. Jiwoo: "Ben… look! It’s in your pocket!" (벤… 봐요! 주머니 안에 있어요!)
9. Ben: "Ha! Thanks, Jiwoo!" (하하! 고마워요, 지우!)
10. Jiwoo: "You’re welcome!" (천만에요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): role reading of that scene.

steps.title: Ben’s Key · 벤의 거실에서

lines.en: Ben… look! It’s in your pocket!

steps.teach:
Role reading of the same scene. The learner is Jiwoo; you read the lines of Ben exactly as written, word for word. Never change, add or skip a line, and never read the learner's lines for them first.
1. Ben (you): "Oh no. Where is my key?" (아이고. 내 열쇠 어디 있지?)
2. Jiwoo (learner): "Is it on the table?" (탁자 위에 있어요?)
3. Ben (you): "No." (아니요.)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "Is it under the sofa?" (소파 밑에는요?)
5. Ben (you): "No…" (아니요…)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Is it on the shelf?" (선반 위는요?)
7. Ben (you): "No! Where is it?" (아니요! 어디 있는 거지?)
8. Jiwoo (learner): "Ben… look! It’s in your pocket!" (벤… 봐요! 주머니 안에 있어요!)
9. Ben (you): "Ha! Thanks, Jiwoo!" (하하! 고마워요, 지우!)
10. Jiwoo (learner): "You’re welcome!" (천만에요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Ben. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.

head: 위치
뜻
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: Where is my ___? / It’s on / under / in the ___. Table (위치 → 뜻):
- on → 위에
- under → 아래에
- in → 안에
- next to → 옆에
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
*on* the desk 책상 위에(붙어서)
*under* the bed 침대 밑에
*in* the bag 가방 안에

서로 알고 있는 물건 앞에 *the*를 붙여요.
It’s on *the* table. (여기 있는 그 탁자)
errors: under만으로 ‘~ 아래에’라는 뜻이라 앞에 in을 붙이지 않아요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- on · under · in: on the desk 책상 위에(붙어서) / under the bed 침대 밑에 / in the bag 가방 안에
- the: 서로 알고 있는 물건 앞에 the를 붙여요. / It’s on the table. (여기 있는 그 탁자)
Common mistakes on screen:
- It’s on table. → It’s on the table. (the를 빼지 않아요.)
- Where my key? → Where is my key? (is를 넣어요.)
- It’s in under the bed. → It’s under the bed. (under만으로 ‘~ 아래에’라는 뜻이라 앞에 in을 붙이지 않아요.)
- You welcome. → You’re welcome. (You’re = You are.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.teach:

items:

2. Jiwoo (learner): "I don’t know. Is it sunny?" (모르겠어요. 맑아요?)
3. Ben (you): "Nope. It’s cloudy today. Look at those clouds." (아니요. 오늘 흐려요. 저 구름 좀 봐요.)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "Oh no. Is it cold?" (어머. 추워요?)
5. Ben (you): "A little. And rain is coming. Take an umbrella!" (조금요. 그리고 비가 올 거예요. 우산 챙겨요!)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Thanks, Ben!" (고마워요, 벤!)
7. Ben (you): "No worries. Don’t get wet!" (별말씀을요. 비 맞지 말아요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Ben. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick true/false check about the scene.

2. It’s a little cold.

head: 날씨
이렇게 말해요
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: How’s the weather today? / It’s ___ today. Table (날씨 → 이렇게 말해요):
- sunny 맑은 → It’s sunny today.
- cloudy 흐린 → It’s cloudy today.
- raining 비가 오는 → It’s raining.
- snowing 눈이 오는 → It’s snowing.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
*It’s* hot. *It’s* cloudy.
여기서 it은 ‘날씨’예요. 따로 뜻은 없어요.

It’s rain*ing*. 지금 비가 와요.
It’s snow*ing*. 지금 눈이 와요.
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- 날씨는 It’s로: It’s hot. It’s cloudy. / 여기서 it은 ‘날씨’예요. 따로 뜻은 없어요.
- 지금 오는 비·눈은 -ing: It’s raining. 지금 비가 와요. / It’s snowing. 지금 눈이 와요.
Common mistakes on screen:
- Today is rain. → It’s raining today. (날씨는 It’s로 시작해요.)
- Weather is hot. → It’s hot. (It’s 하나로 충분해요.)
- It’s rain. → It’s raining. / It’s rainy. (rain은 ‘비’, raining은 ‘비가 오는 중’.)
- Take a umbrella. → Take an umbrella. (umbrella는 모음 소리라서 an.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) sunny / hot → It’s sunny and hot today.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) sunny / hot → It’s sunny and hot today. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: sunny → hot | cloudy → cool | raining → cold | snowing → very cold.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

This is the start of session 2 of "How’s the weather today?" (오늘 날씨); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "How’s the weather today?" / "It’s ___ today." / "Take an umbrella!". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:

steps.title: Rainy Day

steps.title: 시간 돼요?
steps.scene_desc: 동네 카페 창가. 대니얼이 서울 지도를 펼쳐 보이며 무언가를 제안하고, 지우가 휴대폰 달력을 확인하는 모습
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Are you free on Saturday?" (시간 돼요?). Goal: 시간이 되는지 묻고 답하기(가상 약속). Today's scene: 동네 카페 창가. 대니얼이 서울 지도를 펼쳐 보이며 무언가를 제안하고, 지우가 휴대폰 달력을 확인하는 모습. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Are you free on ___?".

steps.when: 약속을 잡을 때 시간이 되는지 물어요.
steps.teach:

Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "Yes, I’m free. / Sorry, I’m busy.".

steps.scene_desc: 토요일, 동네 공원 테니스장 옆. 테니스 라켓을 든 마야가 지우에게 라켓을 건네고, 지우는 손사래를 치며 웃음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Can you swim?" (할 수 있어요). Goal: 할 수 있는 것과 없는 것을 묻고 말하기. Today's scene: 토요일, 동네 공원 테니스장 옆. 테니스 라켓을 든 마야가 지우에게 라켓을 건네고, 지우는 손사래를 치며 웃음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "Can you ___?".

Expression 1 of 3: "Can you ___?" (~할 줄 알아요?). When to use it: 할 수 있는지 물어요. Note: Can you swim?
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I can ___.".

steps.title: 우리 집
steps.scene_desc: 지우의 새 방. 문을 열어 그레이스를 맞이하는 지우. 침대·책상·스탠드, 큰 창문 두 개, 아직 커튼은 없음. 그레이스가 작은 화분을 들고 있음
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "Come in!" (우리 집). Goal: 집과 방에 무엇이 있는지 말하기. Today's scene: 지우의 새 방. 문을 열어 그레이스를 맞이하는 지우. 침대·책상·스탠드, 큰 창문 두 개, 아직 커튼은 없음. 그레이스가 작은 화분을 들고 있음. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "There’s a ___ in my room.".

Expression 1 of 3: "There’s a ___ in my room." (제 방에 ~가 있어요.). When to use it: 무엇이 있는지 말해요(하나). Note: There’s = There is.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "There are two ___s.".

Expression 2 of 3: "There are two ___s." (~가 두 개 있어요.). When to use it: 둘 이상 있을 때 말해요. Note: There are two windows.

What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "Come in!".

steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: There’s a ___ in my room. / There are two ___s. Table (하나 / 둘 이상 → 이렇게 말해요):
- a bed → There’s a bed.
- a lamp → There’s a lamp.
- two windows → There are two windows.
- three chairs → There are three chairs.
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:

- In my room have a bed. → There’s a bed in my room. (‘~가 있어요’는 There’s.)
- There are a sofa. → There’s a sofa. (하나면 is.)

steps.title: 좋아하는 것
steps.title_en: What do you do for fun?
steps.goal: 쉬는 날 즐겨 하는 것을 묻고 말하기
steps.scene_desc: 퇴근길, 회사 앞 횡단보도. 클로이가 휴대폰으로 한국 드라마 장면을 보여 주며 신나 하고, 지우가 웃으며 들여다봄
steps.teach:
This is the very start of the class. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up, like a real tutor meeting a student: greet the learner by name (if this is your first class together, introduce yourself as your class notes say). Then have a short, genuine small-talk chat of about two to four exchanges: how they are, their day, the weather, or something you know about them. React to what they actually say with real interest, and share a small, ordinary thing about yourself now and then. Keep it easy for their level; Korean answers are fine here, just respond to them naturally.
2) Then bridge from the chat to today's topic: "What do you do for fun?" (좋아하는 것). Goal: 쉬는 날 즐겨 하는 것을 묻고 말하기. Today's scene: 퇴근길, 회사 앞 횡단보도. 클로이가 휴대폰으로 한국 드라마 장면을 보여 주며 신나 하고, 지우가 웃으며 들여다봄. Link it to something from the chat if you can, and say in a sentence what we'll do: learn 3 expressions, then hear a short scene.
3) Call next_step only after the learner has answered and seems ready.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 1, "What do you do for fun?".

steps.en: What do you do for fun?
steps.teach:
Expression 1 of 3: "What do you do for fun?" (쉴 때 뭐 하고 놀아요?). When to use it: 취미를 물어요. Note: for fun = 재미로.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 2, "I like ___ing.".

steps.extra: I like walking. · I like watching movies.
steps.teach:
Expression 2 of 3: "I like ___ing." (~하는 걸 좋아해요.). When to use it: 즐겨 하는 일을 말해요. Note: I like walking. · I like watching movies.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. The learner fills the blank with their own real word (for example their own name), never by reading the blank. Show it first with your own example. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): expression 3, "That’s cool!".

Expression 3 of 3: "That’s cool!" (멋지네요!). When to use it: 상대 이야기에 반응해요. Note: 친근한 말이에요.
Teach it like a person, not a drill: set up a tiny real situation (from the warm-up chat or the learner's life if you can), say it, and let the learner say it. Then really use it together in a short exchange: you each say something, and you answer as yourself (if the learner asks you a question, answer it honestly in a natural way). Fix at most one thing, gently. When they have used it once in that exchange and you have replied to them, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): the app plays a short scene ("After Work · 퇴근길에") in the characters' own voices — tell them to just listen.

lines.en: Jiwoo, {{what do you do for fun}}?

steps.teach:
The app has just played this scene, "After Work · 퇴근길에", in the characters' own voices. The learner heard it and sees it on screen:

4. Jiwoo: "That’s cool! Do you understand them?" (멋지다! 다 알아들어요?)
5. Chloe: "A little! I learn Korean from dramas. Listen: “Daebak!”" (조금요! 드라마로 한국어를 배워요. 들어 봐요. “대박!”)
6. Jiwoo: "Ha! Your Korean is great." (하하! 한국어 잘하네요.)
7. Chloe: "Ooh, thanks! I like listening to music, too." (오, 고마워요! 음악 듣는 것도 좋아해요.)

9. Chloe: "K-pop and classical music!" (케이팝이랑 클래식이요!)
Talk about it like a person: a short natural reaction, then one simple question about what happened (the answer is in the lines above). React to their answer; if it is not right, point kindly to the line that shows it. Then call next_step.

3. Chloe (you): "I like watching Korean dramas!" (저는 한국 드라마 보는 걸 좋아해요!)
4. Jiwoo (learner): "That’s cool! Do you understand them?" (멋지다! 다 알아들어요?)
5. Chloe (you): "A little! I learn Korean from dramas. Listen: “Daebak!”" (조금요! 드라마로 한국어를 배워요. 들어 봐요. “대박!”)
6. Jiwoo (learner): "Ha! Your Korean is great." (하하! 한국어 잘하네요.)
7. Chloe (you): "Ooh, thanks! I like listening to music, too." (오, 고마워요! 음악 듣는 것도 좋아해요.)

9. Chloe (you): "K-pop and classical music!" (케이팝이랑 클래식이요!)
First say in one short sentence that they will be Jiwoo and you will read Chloe. Then go in order, one line at a time: call highlight_line with the line number before each line, read your line, and for the learner's line just wait for them to say it. If they say only part of it, say that line once and let them try once more, then go on. After the last line, give one short warm comment on how they did, then call next_step.

items: Jiwoo likes walking in the park.
steps.teach:

1. Jiwoo likes walking in the park.
2. Chloe learns Korean from dramas.

The scene they are about:

2. Jiwoo: "I like walking in the park. And you?" (공원 걷는 거 좋아해요. 클로이는요?)
3. Chloe: "I like watching Korean dramas!" (저는 한국 드라마 보는 걸 좋아해요!)
4. Jiwoo: "That’s cool! Do you understand them?" (멋지다! 다 알아들어요?)
5. Chloe: "A little! I learn Korean from dramas. Listen: “Daebak!”" (조금요! 드라마로 한국어를 배워요. 들어 봐요. “대박!”)
6. Jiwoo: "Ha! Your Korean is great." (하하! 한국어 잘하네요.)
7. Chloe: "Ooh, thanks! I like listening to music, too." (오, 고마워요! 음악 듣는 것도 좋아해요.)

Before you judge an answer, check the scene lines carefully: who said what. Ask one statement at a time: read it yourself and ask True or false?. Accept true/false, yes/no, or Korean (맞아요/아니에요). Say whether they are right and point to the line that shows it in a few words, also when they are right. In Korean say the answer as 정답은 True예요 / 정답은 False예요. There are 3 statements: ask every one and wait for an answer to each (Oh or Hmm is not an answer). Only after you have checked the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a table of useful sentences for real situations.

frame: What do you do for fun?
head: 동사
-ing
이렇게 말해요
rows: I like walking in the park.
steps.teach:
Useful sentences on screen. Key pattern: What do you do for fun? / I like ___ing. Table (동사 → -ing):
- watch 보다 → watching
- walk 걷다 → walking
- listen 듣다 → listening
- play 하다 → playing
Turn two or three rows into quick real-life moments, one at a time (for example: You meet a new neighbor. What do you ask?), let the learner answer, and react to what they say like a person. One task per turn. Do not read labels, arrows or the word pattern aloud. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short grammar point and common mistakes.

items:
‘~하는 걸 좋아해요’
I like read*ing*. I like cook*ing*.

watch → watching
run → run*n*ing(자음 하나 더)
dance → danc*ing*(e 빼고)
errors: 이 과에서는 like + -ing를 연습해요. (like to watch도 맞아요)
What do you do for fun?
steps.teach:
Grammar on screen:
- like + 동사-ing: ‘~하는 걸 좋아해요’ / I like reading. I like cooking.
- -ing 만들기: watch → watching / run → running(자음 하나 더) / dance → dancing(e 빼고)
Common mistakes on screen:
- I like watch movies. → I like watching movies. (이 과에서는 like + -ing를 연습해요. (like to watch도 맞아요))
- I like listen music. → I like listening to music. (listen 뒤에는 to.)
- What do you do fun? → What do you do for fun? (for를 빼지 않아요.)
- I like play soccer. → I like playing soccer. (-ing를 붙여요.)
Explain each point in one or two plain sentences with a short example, ideally about the learner. Then pick two of the mistakes: say the wrong sentence, let the learner fix it, and confirm. Keep it light, then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a quick situation drill.

steps.note: 예) read → I like reading.
steps.teach:
Drill. How it works (note on screen): 예) read → I like reading. Items, each a pair of cues the learner uses to build the answer: read → 책 읽기 | cook → 요리하기 | play soccer → 축구하기 | take photos → 사진 찍기.
First read the example in the note: it shows exactly what the learner says for one item and who plays which role (sometimes the learner speaks as the named person, for example they pretend to be Daniel and introduce themselves as Daniel; sometimes you play a role and answer). Set up each item in one short English sentence so the expected answer is clear and matches the example, let the learner answer, and react. Recast once if needed. There are 4 items: do every one, one per turn, in order. Only after the last answer, call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): wrapping up today.

Wrap up session 1 like a person ending a class. Ask in one short question how today's class felt, and react to their answer. Then praise one specific thing they did today, say that next time we will learn more expressions on this topic and talk about their own story, and say a warm goodbye (use today's expression if it fits). Call finish_session only at the end of that goodbye reply, after you have said all of it.

cards: What do you do for fun?
steps.teach:
This is the start of session 2 of "What do you do for fun?" (좋아하는 것); it may be a different day from session 1. Do not start the textbook yet.
1) Warm-up: greet the learner by name and have a short, genuine small-talk chat of two or three exchanges (how they have been, or follow up on something they told you before). React to what they say.
2) Then bridge to a quick review of last time's expressions: "What do you do for fun?" / "I like ___ing." / "That’s cool!". For each, give a tiny real situation and let them answer; react naturally. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): more expressions on the same topic.

More expressions on this topic (on screen):
- 취미 말하기: "I like watching movies." (영화 보는 걸 좋아해요., 보통); "I play games." (게임을 해요., 보통); "I listen to music." (음악을 들어요., 보통)
- 더 묻기: "What kind of music?" (어떤 음악이요?, 보통); "Really?" (정말요?, 친근)
- 반응하기: "Me, too!" (저도요!, 친근); "Not me." (저는 아니에요., 친근); "Let’s do it together." (같이 해요., 친근); "That’s cool!" (멋지네요!, 친근)
Do not read the whole list. Pick three or four that fit the learner's life, say each and let them say it, and use one or two in a quick real exchange with them. Mention casual (친근) vs polite (정중) where it helps. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): tips and a fill-in-the-blank dialogue.

Mention each tip in one or two sentences, linked to the learner if you can. Then do the fill-in-the-blank dialogue: read it line by line, pausing at each blank so they can fill it, and confirm. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): picture words.

Picture words on screen. New: music (음악), game (게임), walk (걷다, 산책), sport (운동), soccer (축구), baseball (야구), photo (사진), program ((TV) 프로그램), watch (보다(새 뜻)). Review words: movie (영화), listen (듣다), book (책).

Word list on screen: fun (재미) — "for fun"; kind (종류(앞에서는 ‘친절한’)) — "What kind of music?"; classical (클래식의) — "classical music"; cool (멋진(앞에서는 ‘시원한’)) — "That’s cool!"; drama (드라마) — "Korean dramas"; park (공원) — "in the park"; play ((게임·운동을) 하다) — "play games"; read (읽다) — "I like reading."; picture (사진, 그림) — "take pictures".
Pick three or four, say their example phrases, then ask the learner to make one short sentence about their own life with one of them, and respond to what they say. Then call next_step.

steps.teach:
My story: this is the most conversational part of the lesson. Questions on screen:
- "What do you do for fun?" (hint on screen: I like ___ing.)
- "Do you like watching dramas?" (hint on screen: Yes, I do. / Not really.)

Ask them one at a time as a real conversation: react to each answer with genuine interest, add a short follow-up question or a bit about yourself when it feels natural, then move on. Ask for a full sentence and recast once if needed. If they don't want to answer, accept that or an imagined answer without asking again. Then call next_step.
What comes next (after you call next_step): a short reading.
